title: Vegetation in Eastern Africa
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Facts: rain forest (Kakamega, western Uganda), savanna (Serengeti, Mara), semi-desert scrub (north Kenya), mountain vegetation in zones, mangroves at the coast. Collect leaves from the school to compare shapes.

skills.key_step: The child names the main vegetation types of Eastern Africa and where each grows.

floor.question: Which climatic region is wet all year?

steps: Read the climate of the place.
Match it to a vegetation type.
Name a place where it grows.

board.do: Draw a coastline with trees standing in water.

board.say: What vegetation grows in salty water at the coast?

board.do: Write each type with a place.

listen_for: The Serengeti and the Maasai Mara
misconceptions.repair: Connect grassland and wildlife: ask where zebra and wildebeest live.
Show a picture of stilt roots in the sea water at the coast.
Ask which plants need the most water.

misconceptions.ask: Which vegetation covers most of Eastern Africa?
misconceptions.repair: Shade the vegetation map: most of it is savanna.

checks.question: Where is savanna grassland found in Kenya?
checks.answer: the Maasai Mara or other grasslands

checks.question: Name a forest in Kenya.
checks.answer: Kakamega Forest or another named forest

skills.key_step: The child describes each vegetation type and links its traits to climate.

floor.question: Name the vegetation of the Serengeti.

steps: Say how it suits the rain.

board.do: Draw a mountain with three bands.

board.say: What grows lowest on the mountain?

board.do: Write forest, bamboo, moorland from bottom up.

misconceptions.repair: Ask how a plant would keep water in a hot, dry place.

listen_for: Thick forest with tall trees close together
misconceptions.repair: Draw the Mara plain with a few acacia trees.

misconceptions.ask: How does vegetation change as you climb Mount Kenya?
misconceptions.repair: Draw the mountain in four bands.

misconceptions.ask: Why do many desert plants have thorns instead of broad leaves?
misconceptions.repair: Put a broad leaf and a thorny twig in the sun and compare after an hour.

checks.question: Describe savanna vegetation.
checks.answer: tall grass with scattered flat-topped trees

checks.question: Why does vegetation change as you climb a mountain?

skills.key_step: The child picks actions that protect vegetation and rejects ones that harm it.

floor.question: What vegetation grows at the coast in salty water?

representations: a photo of a burnt hill
steps: Ask what it does to plants.

listen_for: Burning the bush to clear it
misconceptions.repair: Ask what burning does to soil, animals and young trees.

misconceptions.ask: What happens when a forest is cut for charcoal?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what holds the soil when the trees are gone.

misconceptions.ask: A company cuts 100 trees and plants one. Has it conserved the forest?
misconceptions.repair: Count trees cut and planted on the board.

listen_for: Nothing, it is the government's job
misconceptions.ask: What can a school do to conserve vegetation?
misconceptions.repair: Start or visit the school tree nursery.

checks.question: Give two ways of conserving vegetation.
checks.answer: any two of: plant trees, replant, agroforestry, control fires, avoid overgrazing, energy-saving jikos, laws

checks.question: Does burning charcoal from forest trees conserve vegetation?
